description: Targeted practice supplements for exact previously unassigned published lesson titles; no original lesson records modified.

units.title: Processes, services, and performance clues — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A slow workstation needs evidence-based diagnosis.

sections.heading: Observe resource usage without modifying the system
sections.command: Windows Task Manager → Processes → sort by CPU and Memory
sections.instruction: Record the top process names and resource percentages at two observation times, and compare with the machine's available memory.
sections.interpretation: High CPU or RAM identifies workload pressure, not automatically malware or failing hardware.
sections.task: Create a short incident note separating current measurements from hypotheses.
sections.safety: Do not end unfamiliar system processes or disable security software merely to improve performance.

units.title: PowerShell inspection: processes, services, and safe triage — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A support analyst must identify what is running without stopping services.
units.lesson: PowerShell inspection: processes, services, and safe triage

sections.heading: Inspect running services and process state safely
sections.command: Get-Process | Select-Object -First 10 Name,Id,CPU; Get-Service | Select-Object -First 10 Name,Status
sections.instruction: Use read-only PowerShell process and service queries; process CPU is cumulative CPU time, not an instantaneous percentage.
sections.interpretation: A stopped service may be expected. Correlate startup type, dependencies, and logs before inferring a fault.
sections.task: List two healthy versus suspicious interpretations of the same stopped service.
sections.safety: Use PowerShell only on your own or authorized Windows computer. Do not run scripts from unknown sources.

units.title: RAM selection and upgrade planning — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A 4 GB laptop is slow, and a seller recommends a 16 GB DIMM.

sections.heading: Confirm memory compatibility and budget
sections.command: Task Manager → Performance → Memory; manufacturer service guide
sections.instruction: Check exact model, socket/soldered layout, maximum supported memory, module type and serviceability before purchasing.
sections.interpretation: A single installed memory slot does not prove that 16 GB is supported; extra RAM does not fix a slow CPU.
sections.task: Prepare a compatibility worksheet listing current RAM, supported options and limits.
sections.safety: Disconnect power and follow manufacturer battery/ESD precautions for physical upgrades.

units.title: Storage, SSDs and backup strategy — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A low-storage laptop cannot install a large training image.

sections.heading: Distinguish capacity, media and data protection
sections.command: Settings → System → Storage; File Explorer drive properties
sections.instruction: Compare free capacity, drive type, external backup options, and restore-time goals before selecting storage.
sections.interpretation: An SSD upgrade may help throughput but cannot be assumed possible when the laptop uses embedded eMMC.
sections.task: Design a backup/restore plan for synthetic lab files and record verification steps.
sections.safety: Back up important data before changes; never initialize or format the live system disk during the exercise.

units.title: Power supplies and electrical safety — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A workstation upgrade adds a new GPU but retains an unknown old power supply.

sections.heading: Estimate demand and safe power margin
sections.command: GPU vendor power recommendation; PSU label; motherboard connector checklist
sections.instruction: Estimate component wattage under load and check connector availability, voltage requirements, unit age and quality.
sections.interpretation: A wattage sticker alone does not establish usable rail capacity or electrical safety.
sections.task: Draft a justified PSU selection with safety margin and compatibility evidence.
sections.safety: Never open a power supply enclosure; capacitors can retain dangerous charge after unplugging.

units.title: GPU needs for cybersecurity — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A beginner wants an expensive GPU for Linux administration and virtual machines.

sections.heading: Assess GPU value against the training workload
sections.command: System requirements of local VMs and training tools; GPU memory specification
sections.instruction: Compare RAM, CPU virtualization, SSD storage and graphics needs for the actual coursework.
sections.interpretation: Linux CLI, networking and most defensive labs do not need a high-end GPU; local AI or GPU workloads may.
sections.task: Write a budget trade-off matrix showing more useful upgrades first.
sections.safety: Do not promise accelerated work without verifying tool-specific hardware support.

units.title: Cooling, airflow and thermals — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A desktop slows under moderate load, while its fan reports a warning.

sections.heading: Collect thermal evidence before repair
sections.command: Firmware hardware monitor or manufacturer diagnostic utility
sections.instruction: Record idle and load temperatures and fan behavior under a short, monitored, approved test.
sections.interpretation: High temperature plus low fan speed suggests cooling issues but may also reflect a bad sensor.
sections.task: Prepare a cooling fault tree and a post-repair retest plan.
sections.safety: Stop a test if overheating or thermal shutdown occurs; disconnect power before opening the chassis.

units.title: Compatibility and purchasing exercise — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A student must select components without exceeding a fixed budget.

sections.heading: Build a parts compatibility checklist
sections.command: CPU socket; motherboard chipset; RAM generation; PSU connectors; case clearance
sections.instruction: Check each cross-component constraint and retain links to manufacturer specifications with revision date.
sections.interpretation: A compatible CPU socket is necessary but not always sufficient; BIOS support can still matter.
sections.task: Create a bill of materials with alternatives, availability uncertainty and upgrade path.
sections.safety: Avoid assuming current retail prices or stock without dated verification.

units.title: Hardware inspection and tool safety — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A training PC is ready for authorized internal inspection.

sections.heading: Prepare a no-damage hardware inspection
sections.command: Power off; unplug; confirm internal battery and ESD procedures
sections.instruction: Document power state, external connectors, case condition and approved inspection sequence before handling components.
sections.interpretation: A clean-looking component does not mean it works; physical inspection supplements but doesn't replace diagnostics.
sections.task: Write a checklist for static control, tools, screws, photos and reassembly.
sections.safety: Do not probe energized circuits or open power supplies.

units.title: Windows installation and drivers — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A workstation requires a clean Windows installation, with user data still present.

sections.heading: Plan a safe OS install workflow
sections.command: Windows recovery options; device manufacturer's official driver catalog
sections.instruction: Confirm OS license, recovery path, backups, storage target and driver source before initiating changes.
sections.interpretation: A successful OS boot isn't proof all drivers, security updates and user data are restored.
sections.task: Write an install acceptance checklist with data restore, updates and Device Manager checks.
sections.safety: Do not erase or format a real user's drive as practice.

units.title: Linux installation and dual boot — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A student wants Linux on a small Windows laptop with limited storage.

sections.heading: Compare non-destructive install options
sections.command: wsl --list --verbose; Windows storage free-space view
sections.instruction: Compare WSL 1, WSL 2, bootable live USB and dual boot against RAM, disk and recoverability.
sections.interpretation: WSL 1 is lightweight but not equivalent to a hardened virtual-machine sandbox.
sections.task: Recommend a reversible beginner setup and describe rollback steps.
sections.safety: Never resize or overwrite a personal Windows partition without a verified backup.

units.title: Diagnosing no-POST and no-display faults — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A system turns on without displaying a BIOS logo.

sections.heading: Separate startup failure categories
sections.command: POST beeps/LED codes; external display; firmware health diagnostics
sections.instruction: Use known-good power and display checks, then follow a staged firmware, memory and video diagnostic flow.
sections.interpretation: Power LEDs and spinning fans do not confirm successful POST or OS startup.
sections.task: Make a decision tree with a safe observation and next step for three branches.
sections.safety: Power down before reseating components; follow ESD practices.

units.title: Diagnosing crashes and performance — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A training workstation freezes when a memory-heavy app opens.

sections.heading: Correlate symptom timing with resource and event logs
sections.command: Windows Reliability Monitor; Event Viewer; Task Manager
sections.instruction: Record error timestamps and app/process memory usage, then compare to storage, thermal and driver evidence.
sections.interpretation: A crash event can identify a symptom but seldom proves its ultimate cause.
sections.task: Propose two controlled hypothesis tests and an evidence collection plan.
sections.safety: Don't disable security protections or replace multiple components at once.

units.title: Privacy and ethics in repairing others' PCs — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A friend authorizes hardware repair but has not authorized access to personal documents.
units.lesson: Privacy and ethics in repairing others' PCs

sections.heading: Protect device owner data during repairs
sections.command: Written repair authorization and data-handling checklist
sections.instruction: Define allowed diagnostics, consent scope, data backup handling, and secure reporting before starting.
sections.interpretation: Device possession is not permission to inspect private photos, emails or passwords.
sections.task: Draft repair consent conditions and a data minimization procedure.
sections.safety: Use fictional data; never access personal files outside the explicitly agreed repair scope.

units.title: Laptop vs desktop upgrades — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A compact laptop has one RAM slot and embedded storage.

sections.heading: Distinguish repairable from integrated components
sections.command: Exact model service guide; board images; warranty policy
sections.instruction: Classify RAM, SSD, wireless, battery, cooling and CPU as socketed, replaceable, soldered or manufacturer-service-only.
sections.interpretation: A desktop's upgrade freedom cannot be assumed for laptops.
sections.task: Write a repair-versus-replace recommendation including cost and performance limits.
sections.safety: Inspect the service guide before opening the device, and observe battery safety.

units.title: Repair capstone: diagnose and document — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A customer reports crashes and requests an immediate motherboard replacement.

sections.heading: Complete an evidence-backed service ticket
sections.command: Fault record; controlled tests; change approval; retest observations
sections.instruction: Write intake, reproduce symptoms, eliminate hypotheses one by one, and record outcome with confidence.
sections.interpretation: A part replacement followed by one successful reboot is not enough to establish long-term resolution.
sections.task: Submit a service report including decision rationale, residual uncertainty and next monitoring step.
sections.safety: Use authorized equipment and protect customer information.

units.title: Kali Linux workstation fundamentals — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A learner wants to install a security distribution to run offline tools.
units.course: Red Team Workstation & Home Lab Engineering

sections.heading: Define legitimate workstation roles and boundaries
sections.command: Virtualization plan; operating-system requirements; authorized lab scope
sections.instruction: List tool categories, package provenance, updates, user permissions and why a dedicated practice environment is useful.
sections.interpretation: Installing Kali Linux does not by itself provide authorization or isolation from other systems.
sections.task: Draft a workstation provisioning checklist with rollback and least-privilege controls.
sections.safety: On a low-resource WSL 1 laptop, use approved offline exercises instead of running vulnerable services.

units.title: Windows domain simulation — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A student wants to understand Windows domain users and group policy.
units.course: Red Team Workstation & Home Lab Engineering

sections.heading: Design a fictional identity lab
sections.command: Synthetic OU, account and group policy diagram
sections.instruction: Draw a domain controller, member workstation, service account and user roles, defining intended trust boundaries.
sections.interpretation: A domain can demonstrate central identity; it is not a license to test real corporate environments.
sections.task: Create a role matrix and describe one authorized and one denied access test.
sections.safety: Use a fully isolated training domain and synthetic identities only.

units.title: Linux and web practice targets — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A future lab hosts a deliberately vulnerable training web application.
units.course: Red Team Workstation & Home Lab Engineering

sections.heading: Choose isolated targets for skill progression
sections.command: Two separate VM diagrams; internal-only adapter settings
sections.instruction: Define instructor target and analyst roles, permitted ports, snapshots and stop conditions before launch.
sections.interpretation: A localhost address or a private IP alone does not prove safe containment.
sections.task: Produce an isolation acceptance checklist with adapter, routing and firewall tests.
sections.safety: Do not host intentionally vulnerable targets on WSL 1 connected to real networks.

units.title: Managed switches and VLANs — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A training network separates simulated analyst and target zones.
units.course: Red Team Workstation & Home Lab Engineering

sections.heading: Reason about segmentation without touching real switches
sections.command: Network diagram with VLAN 10 analyst, VLAN 20 target
sections.instruction: Identify VLAN membership, trunk links, routing policies and where isolation enforcement occurs.
sections.interpretation: VLANs alone do not replace firewall policies; inter-VLAN routing may reconnect segments.
sections.task: Specify an allowed and denied traffic matrix for a fictional managed switch.
sections.safety: Do not change household or corporate switch configurations without owner approval.

units.title: Storage, backups, and recovery — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A VM update corrupts the training target, but a snapshot exists.
units.course: Red Team Workstation & Home Lab Engineering

sections.heading: Establish rollback-ready lab operations
sections.command: Snapshot manifest; backing storage capacity; restore test report
sections.instruction: Compare snapshots, independent backups, configuration-as-code and periodic restore validation.
sections.interpretation: A snapshot may depend on the original disk; it is not necessarily an independent backup.
sections.task: Write a recovery sequence with verification of VM isolation after restore.
sections.safety: Use synthetic training data and keep backup copies off public repositories.

units.title: Red Team lab exercise workflow — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A student is given written authorization for a fictional web target.
units.course: Red Team Workstation & Home Lab Engineering

sections.heading: Design a scoped technical assessment process
sections.command: Scope sheet; hypothesis; evidence; fix; retest forms
sections.instruction: Sequence preflight authorization, baseline observations, approved testing, recording and remediation validation.
sections.interpretation: A successful technical request is not a complete security assessment or certified finding.
sections.task: Write a workflow showing an evidence checkpoint and a stop condition at each stage.
sections.safety: Never test real external systems without explicit permission.

units.title: Infrastructure capstone blueprint — practical fieldwork
units.scenario: A learner plans a future two-VM cyber range but currently has 4 GB RAM.
units.course: Red Team Workstation & Home Lab Engineering

sections.heading: Design a budget-conscious safe lab blueprint
sections.command: Host resource table; network adapter map; clean image inventory
sections.instruction: Budget for guest memory, host headroom, disk, CPU virtualization and network isolation.
sections.interpretation: A plan that fits disk but exceeds available RAM will not produce reliable concurrent VMs.
sections.task: Prepare a two-phase blueprint: WSL file exercises now, private two-VM lab after hardware upgrade.
sections.safety: Keep vulnerable targets powered down until independent isolation checks pass.
